name: Can I live in my house during a kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: Can I stay in my house during a kitchen remodel, and what temporary setup do I need?
mainEntity.text: Can I stay in my house during a kitchen remodel, and what temporary setup do I need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Living in the house during a kitchen remodel is possible, but it takes planning and realistic expectations. The kitchen will likely be unusable during demolition, plumbing, electrical, and cabinet installation, so a temporary setup should be arranged in advance. Many homeowners use a laundry room, garage, or dining area with a small refrigerator, microwave, and basic prep surface. Dust containment matters just as much as convenience because kitchen demolition can spread debris through the home quickly. If the remodel involves structural changes or a long lead time for cabinets and counters, the disruption can last longer than expected. A contractor should explain the daily impact before work begins so you can decide whether to stay or temporarily relocate.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many homeowners live in the house during a kitchen remodel, but cooking access will be limited or unavailable for part of the project. A temporary kitchen usually needs a sink alternative, microwave, fridge access, and a protected area for prep. Dust control and clear work zones are essential.
